page.subtitle: Format / model / rate-limit settings shared by all agents. Click a card to edit it; the starred card is the active profile.
page.empty: No model profiles yet — click "Create" in the top right to add the first one.

health.noKeyHint: No API Key set; cannot be called

pool.title: LLM Pool · Failover
pool.description: When enabled, an Agent without a pinned model automatically fails over to the next config when the current one is unusable (insufficient balance / dead Key / rate limiting / service error).
pool.enableHint: Off by default. When off, only the active profile is ever used and a failure stays a failure.
pool.bindFallback: Also fall back when a pinned config fails
pool.bindFallbackHint: Off by default: when an Agent or task pins a config, only that config is used and a failure stays a failure (no silent switch to another model). When enabled, a failing pinned config also falls back to the pool chain below.
pool.notEnough: Only {count} usable profile(s) right now, so the pool has no effect — at least 2 usable profiles (API Key set, or Ollama) with pool participation are required.
pool.recoverNowTitle: Recover now: clears the breaker so the next call retries this profile
pool.explanation: The active profile is always first; the rest follow priority from high to low (set per profile). After a failure a profile enters a cooldown (60s → 5min → 30min), is skipped while cooling down, and switches back automatically once recovered. Profiles whose context window cannot fit the current request are skipped. Agents and tasks with a pinned model do not join the pool by default.

profile.fillNameModel: Please fill in a name and a model
profile.created: Created: {name} (use "Set as active" on its card to enable it)
profile.savedActive: Saved; the active profile takes effect immediately, no restart needed
profile.keyOllamaPlaceholder: optional — a local Ollama server runs keyless
profile.keySetPlaceholder: Set ({hint}); leave empty to keep it
profile.descNew: New profiles are not activated automatically; use 'Set as active' on its card to enable it.
profile.descEdit: Click save after editing; saving the active profile takes effect immediately for all agents.
profile.name: Name
profile.loadModelsTitle: Load available models from the API
profile.proxyHint: Only outbound LLM requests go through this proxy; http/https/socks5 are supported, optionally with credentials (e.g. socks5://user:pass@host:port — URL-encode the password if it contains special characters). Leave empty for no proxy (direct connection).
profile.sessionHeaderHint: Once a header name is set, every request carries this HTTP header, with the value filled in automatically as the current session's session id (chat sessions like conv-12, workers like exp3-worker-i87). Meant for gateways that do prompt caching / sticky routing on a session-id header; stable across turns of one session, distinct across sessions. Leave empty to not send it.
profile.userAgentHint: Overrides the User-Agent header on every outbound LLM request. Useful for gateways that route or allow-list by User-Agent. Leave empty to keep the default User-Agent unchanged.
profile.rateHint: Rate limits of 0 mean unlimited, shared across all agents. The context window is in K (thousand tokens); 0 = the 200K default, capped at 1000 (i.e. 1M). Setting it too high keeps compression from ever triggering.
profile.poolPriorityHint: Higher numbers are picked first; the active profile is always first regardless of this value. Profiles with equal priority take turns leading, spreading quota naturally.
profile.excludedHint: When enabled, this profile is never used as a failover target (Agents / tasks can still pin it explicitly). Suited to expensive profiles reserved for one specific Agent that should not be burned through by other agents' failures.
profile.streamingHint: On (default) streams over SSE, with live in-flight progress and real-time token counting. Off uses true non-streaming (stream:false, returning the full response in one shot) — a way around gateways with broken SSE implementations (empty frames / dropped thinking-field frames), at the cost of losing live in-flight progress.
profile.outputCapHint: How many tokens a single reply may generate at most; sent with every request. 0 (default) = the field is not sent, leaving it to the server default. This is not the same thing as the "context window" above: that is the model's total capacity, used only locally to compute the compression threshold. Set it too low and a reasoning model gets truncated mid-thinking, unable to emit even a one-word answer.
profile.thinkingSwitchHint: Controls whether the thinking field is sent. Not sent = the field is omitted (compatible with models like MiniMax that lack support); Disabled = send disabled; Enabled = send enabled. Independent of the effort below.
profile.thinkingEffortHint: A separate effort knob (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Anthropic output_config.effort). Some APIs have no thinking field and activate thinking via effort alone, so it can be set on its own without sending the thinking switch.

capFieldHint.openai: Which key carries the cap. max_tokens is the default and the vast majority of compatible gateways only accept it; OpenAI's official reasoning models (the o series / GPT-5) conversely only accept max_completion_tokens and fail outright with unsupported_parameter when they receive max_tokens.
capFieldHint.anthropic: Only selectable for the openai format. Anthropic's field name is fixed as max_tokens.
capFieldHint.openai-responses: Only selectable for the openai format. The Responses API's field name is fixed as max_output_tokens.
capFieldHint.ollama: Only selectable for the openai format. Ollama's field name is fixed as max_tokens.

overrides.title: Retry overrides
overrides.description: Applies only to this profile, overriding the global defaults from "Retry & backoff". Each field left empty = follow the global; attempts -1 = disable this layer; a filled interval replaces the exponential backoff with a fixed one. The breaker and intent rerun are process-level and can only be tuned on the global page.

panel.saved: Saved; takes effect immediately (calls already in flight still use the old parameters)
panel.intro: A failed model call passes through five retry layers in turn, innermost to outermost: connect → empty response → same-provider safe window → pool breaker → intent rerun. An outer layer only gets what the inner ones exhausted, so the attempt counts multiply — max out every layer and a single hiccup can burn dozens of requests. Leaving everything empty keeps the current defaults, identical to the behavior before this page existed. The first three layers can be overridden per model profile.

connect.title: Connect retry
connect.trigger: Cannot connect or no 200 yet: network-layer errors such as connection reset / read-write timeout / DNS failure, plus HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.
connect.skips: The remaining status codes (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422 etc.) are deterministic rejections — resending fails the same way, so they bubble up directly.
connect.desc: Resends the same request verbatim. Once the stream has started (a 200 was received), a mid-stream drop is no longer this layer's business.
connect.offHint: -1 = no retries at all; the failure bubbles up immediately

empty.title: Empty-response retry
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 with a normal stop finish_reason, yet not a single content block in the response — gateway empty frames, dropped thinking-field frames and sampling hiccups all look like this.
empty.skips: Empty because of max_tokens truncation does not count (fix that by raising the output cap; resending just hits it again).
empty.desc: Resends the entire prompt, so it is relatively expensive on long contexts; keep the count small.
empty.offHint: -1 = hand the empty response through as-is

stream.title: Same-provider safe-window retry
stream.where: This project · before any output is delivered
stream.trigger: Trouble only after the stream is established (a 200 received): mid-stream disconnects, provider overloaded, in-stream 429 / 5xx error events — while not a single token has been handed to the caller yet.
stream.skips: Quota exhausted (402 / insufficient_quota, handed to the pool to switch configs), context too long (413 / context length, handed to compression), and deterministic rejections (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422) are never retried.
stream.desc: Replays the same request on the same config. Since no output has been delivered yet, the replay cannot duplicate model output or tool executions.
stream.offHint: -1 = a broken stream goes straight to the outer intent rerun

breaker.title: Pool breaker
breaker.where: This project · process-level, one global copy
breaker.trigger: Trips when transient failures (429, 5xx, network errors) accumulate consecutively to the threshold; deterministic failures — insufficient balance (402), dead key (401 / 403), missing model (404) — ignore the threshold and trip on the first occurrence.
breaker.skips: One success resets the counter, so an occasionally flaky config is not slowly ground into tripping.
breaker.desc: After tripping it enters cooldown, and while cooling the pool skips the config outright. State is persisted, surviving restarts.
breaker.offHint: -1 = transient failures never trip (deterministic failures still do)

intent.title: Intent rerun
intent.where: This project · process-level, one global copy
intent.trigger: The earlier layers could not save it: the worker ends with model_error — inner retries all exhausted, or the stream broke only after output delivery had started (when replay is unsafe and only a full rerun works).
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is already handled by the pool switching configs and is not rerun here; when the task is paused / aborted / wrapping up it yields immediately, spending no backoff time.
intent.desc: Reruns the whole intent from scratch. It is the outermost layer, so one rerun multiplies the inner layers' attempt counts once more.
intent.offHint: -1 = no rerun; the intent is marked blocked outright
